back: C non-metal; Si, Ge metalloids (semiconductors); Sn, Pb metals.
C, Si, Ge giant covalent: high, falling as bonds weaken; Sn, Pb metallic: much lower.
Diamond: no mobile electrons, insulator. Graphite: one delocalised electron per C, conducts along layers.
Conductivity between metal and insulator that increases with temperature (Si, Ge).
Diamond: cutting tools, drill bits, jewellery (hard). Graphite: pencils, lubricant, electrodes (soft layers, conducts).
Si: chips, solar cells (semiconductor). SiO₂: glass, ceramics (high melting point, hard).
Tin: plating food cans, bronze, solder, pewter. Lead: lead-acid batteries, radiation shielding.
Former solvent and fire-extinguisher fluid; now restricted: toxic and ozone-depleting.
SiO₂ + 2C → Si + 2CO (electric furnace); then purified for electronics.
